mcqs.question: What distinguishes edge compute from a CDN?
options: Edge compute runs small, constrained functions per request at the same locations a CDN uses to cache and serve content
A CDN runs full application code; edge compute only caches static files
Edge compute and a CDN are two names for exactly the same service
A CDN only exists in a single cloud region, while edge compute is globally distributed
mcqs.explanation: Edge compute layers request-time logic onto the same distributed points of presence a CDN uses for caching — the CDN itself has no compute capability, and edge compute is not full application hosting.

mcqs.question: Why does running a function at an edge point of presence reduce latency compared to a central cloud region?
options: Edge CPUs execute instructions faster than data-center CPUs
It reduces the physical network distance, and thus transit time, between the user and the compute — not the speed of computation itself
Edge locations use a different, inherently faster version of the internet backbone
Cloud regions do not have any CPUs dedicated to request processing
mcqs.explanation: The latency win is geographic, not computational — the same code runs at the same speed, just physically closer to the user, cutting network transit time.

mcqs.question: Why do edge runtimes typically enforce short execution time limits?
options: To reduce the provider's electricity costs at each location
Edge functions are billed by the calendar month rather than by execution time
A slow function blocks every request routed through that shared point of presence, so tight limits protect other tenants and requests
Execution time limits are a legal requirement in most countries
mcqs.explanation: Because edge locations are shared, multi-tenant infrastructure serving many requests concurrently, a long-running function would degrade service for everyone routed through that point of presence.

mcqs.question: A team tries to run a multi-step database transaction directly inside an edge function. What's the likely outcome?
options: It works identically to running the same code on a normal application server
The transaction silently runs at the origin instead, with no code changes required
Edge functions automatically convert database transactions into cached static content
It runs into the edge runtime's tight execution-time, memory, and API constraints, since edge runtimes aren't built for stateful, heavy compute
mcqs.explanation: Edge runtimes are deliberately constrained for fast, stateless, request-scoped logic — heavy stateful work like a multi-step transaction runs straight into those execution and API limits.
